subject: Genetics
title: Lactose Tolerance Revolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lactose Tolerance Revolution.

hook.text: Most adult mammals can't digest milk. But 35% of humans can—thanks to a mutation that appeared 7,500 years ago.

buildup.text: The LCT gene normally shuts off after weaning. A mutation near it kept the gene active into adulthood.

discovery.text: Dairy farming created massive selective pressure. Milk-digesters had 19% more surviving children in some populations.

twist.text: This mutation arose independently in East Africa and Europe. Same solution, different origins.

climax.text: Lactose tolerance is one of the fastest and clearest examples of human evolution—happening within recorded history.

punchline.text: Farming changed our food. Our genes followed.

quiz.question: When did the lactose tolerance mutation appear?
